title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 157 (Company to inform Director Identification Number to Registrar)

content.overview: Section 157 requires every company to, within the prescribed period of receipt of intimation from the director under section 156, furnish the Director Identification Number of all its directors to the Registrar or any other officer or authority as may be specified by the Central Government, in the prescribed form and manner.
content.glance: Company must furnish DINs of its directors to the Registrar within the prescribed period after receiving intimation under s. 156; failure attracts penalty.
content.study: Every company shall, within the prescribed period of receipt of intimation by it of the Director Identification Number of its directors under section 156, furnish the Director Identification Number of all its directors to the Registrar or any other officer or authority as may be specified by the Central Government, with such fees as may be prescribed, in the prescribed form and manner. If a company fails to furnish the DIN as required, the company is liable to a penalty as provided in the section. Current-law framing: confirm intimation under s. 156; check company filing to ROC within prescribed period; state penalty on default.

sections.heading: Who Must File
sections.body: Every company that has received intimation of DIN from its directors under section 156.

sections.heading: What and To Whom
sections.body: Furnish the DIN of all its directors to the Registrar or specified officer/authority.

sections.heading: Time and Form
sections.body: Within the prescribed period of receipt of intimation, in the prescribed form and manner, with prescribed fees.

sections.heading: Penalty
sections.body: Failure to furnish attracts the penalty provided in the section for the company (and, where the section so provides, for officers in default).

provisions.title: Company to inform Director Identification Number to Registrar

examples.title: Compliant filing
examples.body: Directors intimate DINs under s. 156. The company files the DINs with the Registrar in the prescribed form within the prescribed period under s. 157.

examples.title: Default
examples.body: The company receives DIN intimations but does not file with the ROC within the prescribed period. Section 157 penalty is engaged.

hypotheticals.question: Is the company’s ROC filing duty independent of the director’s intimation duty?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes in structure: s. 156 binds the director; s. 157 binds the company after intimation. In practice the company filing depends on receiving the intimation.

distinctions.title: Company to inform ROC (s. 157) vs director to intimate company (s. 156)
distinctions.left: Company’s duty to file DINs with the Registrar
distinctions.right: Director’s duty to tell the company the DIN

misconceptions.trap: Director’s intimation to the company under s. 156 satisfies the ROC filing requirement.
misconceptions.correction: Section 157 is a separate company duty to furnish DINs to the Registrar after receiving intimation.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 157 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm intimation under s. 156. II. Check company filing to ROC within prescribed period. III. Apply penalty on default. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Intimation facts; filing status; timeline; penalty if any; precise relief.

examTips: Company files with ROC after s. 156 intimation.
